guard_streams.source: Project Gigabit National Rolling Open Market Review May 2026
guard_streams.write_limit: Open Market Review submissions describe supplier-reported existing and planned build over a three-year horizon; they require formal assessment and exact UPRN/current-service validation before any parcel promotion.

facts.detail: The May 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review was published on 1 May 2026.
The consultation page was last updated on 1 June 2026.
The consultation is marked as concluded.
All suppliers were asked to submit information.
The request covered existing and planned build at premises level.
Planned build was requested over the next three-year period.
The request applied across the UK.
The consultation ran from 3pm on 1 May to 5pm on 1 June 2026.
BDUK states that the NR OMR takes place in January, May and September.
The review confirms where gigabit-capable infrastructure exists or is planned.

guard_streams.source: Closure of the May 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review
guard_streams.write_limit: The closure notice records an assessment workflow and future publication of postcode and UPRN outputs; it is not itself exact current selected-parcel service evidence.

facts.detail: The closure notice was updated on 1 June 2026.
The May review concluded at 5pm on 1 June 2026.
The next NR OMR was due to launch in September 2026.
The process operates on a four-monthly January, May and September cycle.
It seeks up-to-date existing and three-year planned-build information.
The data supports strategic planning and prioritisation of intervention areas.
The process aims to avoid intervention that disrupts commercial plans.
Collected data informs GigaHubs and Gigabit Voucher eligibility.
Submitted data is formally assessed for England and Wales.
Postcode and UPRN-level outputs are to be published after assessment.

guard_streams.source: Project Gigabit National Rolling Open Market Review January 2026
guard_streams.write_limit: The January review is a dated supplier-submission and planning process; exact regional file, UPRN, schema and current-service validation remain required for parcel promotion.

facts.detail: The January 2026 NR OMR was published on 6 January 2026.
The page was last updated on 10 June 2026.
The consultation is marked as concluded.
All suppliers were asked to submit information.
The request covered existing and planned build at premises level.
The planning horizon covered the next three years.
The review covered the UK.
It ran from 3pm on 6 January to 5pm on 6 February 2026.
BDUK states that the review occurs in January, May and September.
The June update added a link to regional outputs.

guard_streams.write_limit: Voucher eligibility and grant rules support intervention assessment but do not prove a network is built, orderable or measured at a selected parcel.

facts.detail: The voucher information was updated on 16 March 2026.
The scheme is part of Project Gigabit.
It provides grants toward local gigabit-capable connections.
Vouchers can provide up to £4,500 per eligible premises.
Eligibility requires that existing service is below gigabit-capable speed.
Eligibility excludes premises covered by qualifying near-term commercial build.
Eligibility excludes premises within a government-funded Project Gigabit contract.
A voucher project requires at least two eligible premises.
The new service must double sub-50 Mbit/s service or provide at least 100 Mbit/s where current speed exceeds 50 Mbit/s.
Supplier checks and voucher funding follow connection and scheme verification.

guard_streams.write_limit: The evaluation plan describes programme design, research phases and remote public-building interventions; it cannot establish current surrounding-parcel broadband orderability or speed.

facts.detail: BDUK published the Hubs Evaluation Plan on 15 August 2025.
Belmana leads the commissioned evaluation work.
The evaluation team includes Hatch and Winning Moves.
The programme connects remote public buildings such as schools, GP surgeries and libraries.
The plan covers the Rural Gigabit Connectivity programme from 2019 to 2022.
It covers GigaHubs delivery from 2022 to 2026.
The evaluation period runs from 2022 to 2027.
The plan sets out evaluation phases two through four.
The programme value described is £110 million.
The final evaluation report is scheduled for April 2027.
